The TYPECHECK phase is in the interpreter's list but is a no-op there: `walk` calls `setScala(false)` and the checking flag `fortress.compile.typecheck` defaults to false, and `StaticChecker` returns the tree untouched when off. `compile`/`build` set it on. Emitted classfiles stay at version 1.6 because the load-time rewriting pipeline does not maintain stack-map frames and the JVM verifier may fall back to type inference only at that version. ## Name resolution: fortress.source.path

`default_repository/configuration` (overridable via `local_repository/`,
`~/.fortress/`, `./.fortress/`, env vars, or `-D` flags) defines:

    fortress.source.path=;.;${_fr}/LibraryBuiltin;${FORTRESS_AUTOHOME}/Library;${_fr}/test_library

- Leading `;` sets the separator (Windows compat). `.` (cwd!) is searched
  FIRST, then `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin`, then `Library/`.
- `import Foo` finds the first `Foo.fsi`/`Foo.fss` on that path. First hit
  wins — a file earlier on the path silently shadows a later one, and cwd can
  shadow everything (mind where you run from).

`default_repository/caches/` (gitignored):

  between worlds; the main source of cross-world contamination.
- `interpreter_cache/`, `environment_cache/` — interpreter side.

  library components get api-qualified names (`fortress.CompilerBuiltin.jar`).

  ... recommend you delete the Fortress bytecode cache and relink`). These
  sank pluckyporcupine's compiler verdict; they are cache problems, not
  compiler bugs.

  otherwise invisible (cached analysis wins).

  program does NOT emit the builtin-library jars, and the runtime classloader
  then falls back to the **bootstrap stubs** in `ProjectFortress/build/fortress/`

      ../bin/fortress compile ../Library/CompilerSystem.fss

  `Shell.resetRepository()` and compiles the world in dependency order.

  (and three set neither). Harmless on JDK 8 (target defaulted to 8); on
  JDK 11 target defaulted to 11 → v55 classfiles with invokedynamic string
  concat → ASM 3.1's ClassReader (used by `ForeignJava.findClass` for every
  `import java ...`) dies with `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`, failing all

  generated by astgen from `ProjectFortress/astgen/Fortress.ast` (build

  `research/extracts/fortress-websites-wayback.md`.

  container; only commits and pushes persist.

  (and three set neither). Harmless on JDK 8 (target defaulted to 8); on
  JDK 11 target defaulted to 11 → v55 classfiles with invokedynamic string
  concat → ASM 3.1's ClassReader (used by `ForeignJava.findClass` for every
  `import java ...`) dies with `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`, failing all
  compiler-path tests while testSystem stays green. Fixed by pinning
  `target="${javaSourceVersion}"` on all 8 javac tasks (commit fdd4a57c2).
  Diagnosis trick: a 20-line probe compiling against
  `third_party/asm/asm-all-3.1.jar` + `javap -v | grep major` pinpoints
  exactly which classfile ASM chokes on. (Surprise: JDK 11's *platform*
  classes parse fine under `SKIP_DEBUG|SKIP_FRAMES|SKIP_CODE`; it was our
  own freshly compiled v55 output that broke.)
- `default_repository/caches/global.map` is a **tracked** file at the caches
  root, so `rm -rf default_repository/caches/*` deletes tracked content —
  wipe with `rm -rf default_repository/caches/*_cache
  default_repository/caches/logs` instead, or `git checkout` it back.

## Generated code

- AST nodes (`src/com/sun/fortress/nodes/`, 1000+ files),
  `scala_src/nodes/FortressAst.scala`, `Library/FortressAst.fsi/fss` are all
  generated by astgen from `ProjectFortress/astgen/Fortress.ast` (build
  target `makeAST`). They are checked in; ant's uptodate check compares
  mtimes, so a fresh checkout looks current. If scalac errors show arity
  mismatches in `S*Pattern` nodes: `touch ProjectFortress/astgen/Fortress.ast
  && ant compileAll`.
- Parser (`parser/*.java` from Rats! grammars), `precedence_resolver/
  Operators.java` (from unicode data) — same pattern.

## Test harness mechanics

- Targets: `testFast` (unit + compiler suites, ~12 min, excludes interpreter
  system tests), `testSystem` (interpreter, 382 tests, ~2 min),
  `testLibrary`, `testCompiler`, `testNotPassing` (expected failures),
  `testDemos`, nightly variants. Plain-text results land in
  `ProjectFortress/TEST-RESULTS/TEST-<class>.txt`.
- `.test` files (in `compiler_tests/` etc.) are property files driving
  `FileTests`: keys like `compile`, `run`, `tests=`, `compile_err_equals=`
  decide which phases run and what output to expect. `run`-tests execute the
  compiled program via the `bin/run` script in a subprocess.
- To reproduce one interpreter test: `../bin/fortress tests/<Name>.fss`
  (from `ProjectFortress/`). Failures print the real diagnostic that the
  JUnit boilerplate hides.
- Suite runs reset/repopulate `default_repository/caches` — don't interleave
  ad-hoc compiles with a running suite, and don't trust cache state after one.

## Git archaeology techniques

- **The history has a parallel root**: `5a68404` (David Chase, 2012-07-19,
  4372 files) is a parentless import later merged by `575fe64`. Any
  `git log <base>..HEAD -- <file>` therefore lists `5a68404` for almost
  every file — useless for "who changed what since June". Use **content
  comparison** instead: `git diff --quiet <base> HEAD -- <file>` and
  `git show <base>:<file> | cmp - <other-tree>/<file>` (this is how the
  graft's 3-way audit was done; see the graft commit message).
- pluckyporcupine's base = trunk `304f274` (2012-06-12), confirmed by 56/69
  differing files being byte-identical to it.
- The twelve pre-2016 branches are hg named-branch relics; the 2008 research
  branches were squash-merged into trunk, so fine-grained authorship exists
  only on the branch heads. Full survey with per-branch verdicts: see the
  session notes / ask before deleting anything.
- hg conversion quirks: empty "Starting/Closing branch X" marker commits;
  `.hgignore` still in tree; David Chase's 2012-01-20 branch-closing sweep.

## Environment gotchas (cloud container)

- Current rung JDK 25 (`/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64`; 8/11/17/21 also
  gated green); `unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS` or the proxy's trust-store flags
  pollute every JVM fork.
- `web.archive.org` and `labs.oracle.com` are blocked by network policy —
  research PDFs must be uploaded into the session by Pavol. Archived *pages*
  (not PDFs) can be read via the pure.md relay; see the method note in
  `research/extracts/fortress-websites-wayback.md`.
- Gitignored files (e.g. `research/decks/*.pdf`) do not survive the
  container; only commits and pushes persist.

**Precedence verdict (rows 1-4).** Fortress does leave precedence undefined
between some operator families and then demands parentheses
(`basic/operators/precedence.tex:26-32`, the `a + b ∪ c` example), but that rule
does not reach `x[i][j]`, `x[i]^2` or `f()[i]`. Subscripting and superscripting
are one group that `precedence.tex:44-51` explicitly declares left-associative and
higher than every operator below, and `concrete-syntax.tex:937-953` is left-recursive
on `Primary` for both forms; the parser agrees (`Expression.rats:389, 516-543, 627-648`,
and the dumped AST carries both subscripts). So `x[i][j]` and `x[i]^2` are an
**implementation gap**, localised to one argument-list call in the evaluator.
`f()[i]` is the opposite verdict: the grammar admits it, but the spec's own
reassociation procedure (`juxtameaning.tex:156-162`) makes it a static error, and
the interpreter reports that sentence — a **design limit**.

The mathematical register for "the updated value of X"; contrast row 15, where `W_1` is not a name at all. |

**Precedence verdict (rows 1-4).** Fortress does leave precedence undefined
between some operator families and then demands parentheses
(`basic/operators/precedence.tex:26-32`, the `a + b ∪ c` example), but that rule
does not reach `x[i][j]`, `x[i]^2` or `f()[i]`. Subscripting and superscripting
are one group that `precedence.tex:44-51` explicitly declares left-associative and
higher than every operator below, and `concrete-syntax.tex:937-953` is left-recursive
on `Primary` for both forms; the parser agrees (`Expression.rats:389, 516-543, 627-648`,
and the dumped AST carries both subscripts). So `x[i][j]` and `x[i]^2` are an
**implementation gap**, localised to one argument-list call in the evaluator.
`f()[i]` is the opposite verdict: the grammar admits it, but the spec's own
reassociation procedure (`juxtameaning.tex:156-162`) makes it a static error, and
the interpreter reports that sentence — a **design limit**.

reassociation procedure (`juxtameaning.tex:156-162`) makes it a static error, and

| # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |

Not a Fortress defect — recorded because it is the reason run-b's flagship engine is a tape, and because the two shapes are indistinguishable at depth 1. |

## Contested / unsettled

| # | claim | status | class | reproducer | found by | why unsettled |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 83 | `nat`-generic functions mis-unify on a second instantiation when called through an exported API | CONTESTED | implementation gap (claimed) | none saved — blinded's evidence is a transcript timestamp (`17:29`, the `src/MicroGPT.fsi` attempt) | blinded | No minimal reproducer survives, and building an API + component pair here did not isolate it. ## Disagreements resolved

1. **Chained subscripting / indexed power** — ours classified `m[i][j] → (m[i])[j]` as a *design limit* ("grammatical by design in the spec"); Astra and the blinded run called it an *interpreter gap*. **Astra and blinded are right** (rows 1-3): `concrete-syntax.tex:944-950` is left-recursive on `Primary`, `precedence.tex:44-51` puts subscripting and superscripting in one left-associative group, and `Expression.rats` parses both. The failure is `Evaluator.java:1251-1252`. Row 2 adds that it can also be silently wrong, which no source had.
2. **`f()[i]`** — blinded called it a grammar/design limit, and the review's correction of row 1 risked sweeping it in. **Blinded is right** (row 4): `juxtameaning.tex:157-161` makes it a static error and the interpreter quotes that sentence. Rows 1-3 and row 4 are different verdicts about neighbouring syntax.
3. **"The library cannot call the user's `opr +`"** — our sum experiment stated it unconditionally. **Falsified as stated** (rows 30-32): it holds for top-level `opr` declarations, not for functional methods. The important half is that the fallback is *silent*.
4. **`do … end` as a comprehension body** — blinded listed it as unavailable. **Falsified** (row 10).
5. **Transpose** — Astra recorded `transpose(W)` as a word and a remaining departure; the blinded run avoided needing it. **Ours is right** (row 34): the spec's postfix `^T` is declarable and runs.
6. **Both juxtaposition directions** — Astra judged `v M` unavailable; ours reached it via `Rank1 excludes Rank2`; blinded reached it with two plain overloads on unrelated object types. **Blinded's route is the simpler correct one** (row 33); `excludes` is needed only when the carriers share a supertype.
7. **`extends Number`** — Astra and ours agree it is illegal per `traits.tex:228-235`; ours adds that the walk path never enforces it and that the library types then work in full (rows 22, 52). Not a disagreement, a merge: the row needs both halves or it misleads.
8. **`W_1` / italic `W₁`** — the page-template ledger said italic `W₁` is unreachable. **Sharpened** (rows 15, 66): `W_1` is a lexical error, but `w17` renders `w₁₇`; what is unreachable is a *capital-initial* italic subscripted name, because capital-initial names render as type names.
9. **Σ over a user type** — the earliest of our notes recorded "Σ is sealed, impossible". **Retired by all three runs independently** (rows 40-41): impossible by *addition*, routine by *replacement*.
10. **Matrix pasting** — run-b (and its independent worker) recorded that matrix pasting fails, `[ A ; B ]` included; run-b2 recorded that a rank-one paste always fails but a rank-two paste of square blocks works. **Both are half right** (rows 106, 107): a grid with a single row *or* a single column of matrix elements always fails the extent check — `g18` settles the stacked `[ A ; B ]` of square blocks that run-b never reached and its worker inferred — while a 2×2 grid of square blocks pastes correctly and a 2×2 grid of non-square blocks throws `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`. 11. **Matrix unpasting** — run-b classified it as a design limit (the spec's own `\note`), run-b2 as an implementation gap. **run-b is right** (row 108): `basic/matrix-unpasting.tex:15` declares it not yet supported, so it is classified as row 26 is.
12. **Object-member ordering** — run-b called "field/getter/setter before methods" an implementation gap because "the spec's object grammar orders nothing"; run-b2 called it a design limit and cited the grammar. **run-b2 is right** (row 124): `basic/objects.tex:172-176` and `appendices/grammars/concrete-syntax.tex:268-285` order the two groups. The neighbouring rejection of a `property` after a method *is* an implementation gap (row 125), because the same grammar puts `PropertyDecl` in both groups.
13. **Equality of value objects** — run-b read `P(1.0) === P(2.0) : true` as "`===` compares only the dynamic type"; run-b2 found that it compares the fields the object *body* declares, and that a body with none leaves the list empty. **run-b2's reading is right** (row 113), and it is the sharper claim: adding one field declaration makes the comparison work, and the shipped `Just` has none (row 114).
14. **Overloads on unrelated library types** — run-b met the rejection on two `Array` instantiations, run-b2 on `List` next to `Range`, and both classified it as the spec's Meet Rule. Both are right about the rule (row 97) — but the interpreter enforces it only on a cold cache (row 98, new here). Any future disagreement of the form "that program runs for me" should be re-checked with the component's `interpreter_parsed_cache` entry deleted.
15. **`pi`** — run-b's table first said `pi` is not defined and retired that on its own worker's evidence. The ledger keeps only the sharpened form (row 94): absent from the default library, present in the optional `Constants` API as a `FloatLiteral`, and unavailable under its Unicode name.
16. **`do … end` as a comprehension body, re-checked** — item 4 above settled the blinded run's row 14 against ledger row 10; because that blinded table is still in the tree saying the opposite, it was re-run in this pass: `g11` prints `<\|1, 2, 3\|>`. **Row 10 stands.** The `\|\|` half of the same blinded row is row 9, which run-b then completed (item above and row 9's amended note).

content.content:
(* AplCore -- see AplCore.fsi.  The redesign of v1/base/AplCore.fss, promoted to
   the base on 2026-09-13: APL's values are Fortress's OWN arrays, not a wrapper.

   An APL scalar is an RR64; a vector is an Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] from
   array[\RR64\](n); a matrix is an Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] from
   array[\RR64\](r,c) (merged ledger row 57).  Rank is not a field, it is the
   TYPE, and every primitive is an overload family keyed on rank:

       f(x: RR64)                         rank 0
       f[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\])    rank 1
       f[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\])   rank 2

   This works -- and only this spelling works.  Overloading directly on
   Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] against Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] is rejected ("first
   parameters m:[...] and v:[...] are unrelated (neither subtype, excludes, nor
   equal)", r01_native.out), because two instantiations of one generic trait are
   not known to exclude.  Vector and Matrix reach Rank1 and Rank2, which DO
   exclude each other (FortressLibrary.fsi:1072-1076), and the nat is inferred
   from the runtime-built array (r02a_rankover.out).  Parameters are therefore
   Vector/Matrix; RESULTS are Array[\...\], the honest runtime-sized type.

   What the library does for us, for no lines at all: + and - elementwise on
   equal-length vectors and on matrices (Vector.+, Matrix.+), pmul, DOT, m.t(),
   |v|, v[i], m[i,j], u <- v, comprehensions, SUM, PROD, BIG MAX, and a LENGTH
   ERROR by dispatch when the two nats disagree (r09_reduce.out).

   Index origin is 0, as the chapter sets it with its first line, ⎕IO ← 0. *)
component AplCore
export AplCore

(* ------------------------------------------------------------- numbers ---- *)
(* RR64 -> ZZ32 in one line: there is still no narrowing (apl/gaps.md row 10),
   but the floor bracket's ZZ64 stringifies as an integer (row 11) and
   strToInt reads it back.  v1/base/AplCore.fss spent 14 lines on this. *)
aplInt(v: RR64): ZZ32 = strToInt("" (|\ v /|))

aplNegS(v: RR64): RR64 = -v

(* APL's high minus for negatives; integral values print without a fraction *)
aplFmt(v: RR64): String =
    if v < 0.0 then ("¯" aplFmt(-v))
    elif (1.0 (|\ v /|)) = v then ("" (|\ v /|))
    else ("" v) end

aplPad(s: String, w: ZZ32): String = do
    r: String := s
    while |r| < w do r := (" " r) end
    r
  end

(* ------------------------------------------------------- constructors ----- *)
aplVec(n: ZZ32, f: ZZ32 -> RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = array[\RR64\](n).fill(f)
aplMat(r: ZZ32, c: ZZ32, f: (ZZ32,ZZ32) -> RR64): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    array[\RR64\](r,c).fill(f)
aplZilde(): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = array[\RR64\](0)

(* strand notation, built right to left by the grammar: the tail of a strand is
   a scalar when it has one element and a vector when it has more, so one
   overload each and no length bookkeeping in the grammar. *)
aplCons(x: RR64, y: RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
.....
(* ------------------------------------------------- character arrays ------ *)
(* An APL character array is an Array[\Char,ZZ32\].  It may NOT join the numeric
   overload family: a Char vector parameter beside an RR64 one is rejected,
   "at least one pair of parameters must have excluding types"
   (r07_edge.out), because Array1[\Char,0,s\] and Vector[\RR64,s\] are both
   Rank1 and neither excludes the other.  So the character primitives carry
   their own NAMES -- one extra name per primitive that admits characters --
   and APL's DOMAIN ERROR on 'abc'+1 is the numeric family failing to dispatch
   (r08_edge.out, "Failed to find any matching overload"). *)
aplChars(s: String): Array[\Char,ZZ32\] =
    array[\Char\](|s|).fill(fn (i: ZZ32): Char => s[i])
aplShowC[\nat s\](v: Array1[\Char,0,s\]): String =
    if |v| = 0 then "" else (BIG ||[ i <- seq(0 # |v|) ] ("" v[i])) end
aplTallyC[\nat s\](v: Array1[\Char,0,s\]): RR64 = 1.0 |v|


(* ======================================================== rung 2: indexing ==
   See AplCore.fsi for the rule that shapes every signature here.  Three facts
   from s01_ix.fss, all on the native carrier and all load-bearing:

   (a) a library array is MUTABLE through a Vector/Matrix parameter -- v.put(i,x)
       and m.put((i,j),x) -- so APL's indexed and selective assignment are
       in-place puts.  That is what lets an APL variable be a plain lambda
       parameter: the name never has to be rebound (apl gap row 29 says it
       cannot be) and nothing is copied.
   (b) the library's own row view m[1,:] is NOT an AnyVector (merged ledger
       row 54, re-confirmed here over a runtime-sized matrix), so it carries no
       vector algebra; but a 6-line user object extending Vector (row 55) is one,
       and its nat parameters are inferred from the runtime-built matrix.  So
       m[1;] and m[;1] are zero-copy views with the full algebra.
   (c) RR64 excludes Array1 (FortressLibrary.fsi:1435), so a scalar index and a
       vector index are an excluding pair and the rank of an indexed result is
       settled by overload resolution. *)

(* ------------------------------------------------------- row/column views -- *)
object AplRow[\nat r, nat c\](base: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], i: ZZ32) extends Vector[\RR64,c\]
    get(j: ZZ32): RR64 = base.get(i, j)
    put(j: ZZ32, v: RR64): () = base.put((i, j), v)
    init0(j: ZZ32, v: RR64): () = base.init0((i, j), v)
    replica[\U\](): Array1[\U,0,c\] = array1[\U,c\]()
end
object AplCol[\nat r, nat c\](base: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], j: ZZ32) extends Vector[\RR64,r\]
    get(i: ZZ32): RR64 = base.get(i, j)
    put(i: ZZ32, v: RR64): () = base.put((i, j), v)
    init0(i: ZZ32, v: RR64): () = base.init0((i, j), v)
    replica[\U\](): Array1[\U,0,r\] = array1[\U,r\]()
end

(* ---------------------------------------------------- bracket indexing ----- *)
(* An out-of-range index is APL's INDEX ERROR, as a contract violation. *)

(* AplCore -- see AplCore.fsi.  The redesign of v1/base/AplCore.fss, promoted to
   the base on 2026-09-13: APL's values are Fortress's OWN arrays, not a wrapper.

   An APL scalar is an RR64; a vector is an Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] from
   array[\RR64\](n); a matrix is an Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] from
   array[\RR64\](r,c) (merged ledger row 57).  Rank is not a field, it is the
   TYPE, and every primitive is an overload family keyed on rank:

       f(x: RR64)                         rank 0
       f[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\])    rank 1
       f[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\])   rank 2

   This works -- and only this spelling works.  Overloading directly on
   Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] against Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] is rejected ("first
   parameters m:[...] and v:[...] are unrelated (neither subtype, excludes, nor
   equal)", r01_native.out), because two instantiations of one generic trait are
   not known to exclude.  Vector and Matrix reach Rank1 and Rank2, which DO
   exclude each other (FortressLibrary.fsi:1072-1076), and the nat is inferred
   from the runtime-built array (r02a_rankover.out).  Parameters are therefore
   Vector/Matrix; RESULTS are Array[\...\], the honest runtime-sized type.

   What the library does for us, for no lines at all: + and - elementwise on
   equal-length vectors and on matrices (Vector.+, Matrix.+), pmul, DOT, m.t(),
   |v|, v[i], m[i,j], u <- v, comprehensions, SUM, PROD, BIG MAX, and a LENGTH
   ERROR by dispatch when the two nats disagree (r09_reduce.out).

export AplCore

(* ------------------------------------------------------------- numbers ---- *)
(* RR64 -> ZZ32 in one line: there is still no narrowing (apl/gaps.md row 10),
   but the floor bracket's ZZ64 stringifies as an integer (row 11) and
   strToInt reads it back.  v1/base/AplCore.fss spent 14 lines on this. *)

aplNegS(v: RR64): RR64 = -v

(* APL's high minus for negatives; integral values print without a fraction *)
aplFmt(v: RR64): String =
    if v < 0.0 then ("¯" aplFmt(-v))
    elif (1.0 (|\ v /|)) = v then ("" (|\ v /|))
    else ("" v) end

aplPad(s: String, w: ZZ32): String = do
    r: String := s
    while |r| < w do r := (" " r) end

  end

  rank():ZZ32 = n
end

(* Potemkin exclusion traits.  Really we just want to say that
 * Rank[\n\] excludes Rank[\m\] where { m =/= n }, but we can't yet. *)

trait Rank1 extends { Rank[\1\]} excludes { Rank2, Rank3, Number, String }
end

end

trait Rank3 extends { Rank[\3\]} excludes { Number, String }
end

(* The trait Indexed_i[\n\] indicates that something has an i^th
 * dimension of size n.  In general anything which extends Indexed_i
 * must also extend Indexed_j for j < i. *)

trait Indexed1[\ nat n \] extends HasRank end

trait Indexed2[\ nat n \] extends HasRank end

trait Indexed3[\ nat n \] extends HasRank end

(** The indexed trait indicates that an object of type T can be
indexed using type I to obtain elements with type E.

An object i that's an instance of Indexed defines three basic things:
  The indexing operator opr [], which must be defined for every instance of
    the type.

  A suite of generators: i.indices generates the index space of the
    array.  i itself generates the values contained at those indices.
    i.indexValuePairs yields pairs of (index,value).  All of these
    share the same natural order.  It is necessary to define one of
    self.indices and self.indexValuePairs, in addition to generate() (but
    the latter requirement can be dispensed by instead extending
    DelegatedIndexed).

  A set of utility functions, assign, fill, and copy.  Only fill and
    copy need to be defined.
**)
trait Indexed[\E, I\] extends Generator[\E\]
    (** isEmpty indicates whether there are any valid indices.  It is
        defined as size=0 *)
    getter isEmpty(): Boolean = |self| = 0
    getter nonEmpty(): Boolean = NOT self.isEmpty
    (** %self.size% is equivalent to %|self|%. *)
    getter size(): ZZ32 = |self|
    (** self.bounds yields a range of indices that are valid for the
        indexed generator. *)
    getter bounds(): CompactFullRange[\I\]
    (** self.indexValuePairs generates the elements of the indexed object
        (exactly those elements that are generated by the object itself),
        but each element is paired with its index.  When we obtain
        (i,v) from indexValuePairs we know that:
           self[i] = v
           the i are distinct and i IN self.bounds
           stripping away the i yields exactly the results of v <- self
        This generator attempts to follow the structure of the
        underlying object as closely as possible.  *)
    getter indexValuePairs(): Indexed[\(I,E),I\] =
        self.indices.map[\(I,E)\](fn (i:I): (I,E) => (i,self[i]))
    (** reverse gives us an indexed object which is back-to-front:
        the reversed object from the lower bound to the upper bound is the
        original object from upper to lower *)
    getter reverse():Indexed[\E,I\] = SimpleReversedIndexed[\E,I\](self)

        extends { AnyVector, Array1[\T,0,s0\], AdditiveGroup[\Vector[\T,s0\]\] }
        excludes { AnyMultiplicativeRing }
    opr +(self, v:Vector[\T,s0\]): Vector[\T,s0\] =
        ivmap[\T\](fn (i:ZZ32, e: T):T => e + v.get(i))
    opr -(self, v:Vector[\T,s0\]): Vector[\T,s0\] =
        ivmap[\T\](fn (i:ZZ32, e: T):T => e - v.get(i))
    opr -(self): Vector[\T,s0\] = map[\T\](fn (e: T):T => - e)

    pmul(v: Vector[\T,s0\]): Vector[\T,s0\] =

    dot(v: Vector[\T,s0\]): T =

trait Matrix[\T extends Number, nat s0, nat s1\]
        extends { AnyMatrix, Array2[\T, 0, s0, 0, s1\], AdditiveGroup[\Matrix[\T,s0,s1\]\] }
        excludes { AnyMultiplicativeRing }
    opr +(self, v:Matrix[\T,s0,s1\]): Matrix[\T,s0,s1\] =
        ivmap[\T\](fn (i:(ZZ32,ZZ32),e:T):T => e + v.get(i))
    opr -(self, v:Matrix[\T,s0,s1\]): Matrix[\T,s0,s1\] =
        ivmap[\T\](fn (i:(ZZ32,ZZ32),e:T):T => e - v.get(i))
    opr -(self): Matrix[\T,s0,s1\] = map[\T\](fn (e:T):T => - e)
    scale(t1: T): Matrix[\T,s0,s1\] = map[\T\](fn (e:T):T => t1 e)
    mul[\ nat s2 \](other: Matrix[\T,s1,s2\]): Matrix[\T,s0,s2\] = do
        res = matrix[\T,s0,s2\]()
        mma(a:ZZ32,i:ZZ32,b:ZZ32,j:ZZ32,c:ZZ32,k:ZZ32):() =
            if k>=i AND k>=j then
              if k=1 then
                pr : T = get(a,b) other.get(b,c)
                (* If this were atomic, we could parallelize j-partition. *)
                res.put((a,c), res.get(a,c) + pr)
              else
                (k0,k1) = partition(k)
                (mma(a,i,b,j,c,k0),mma(a,i,b,j,c+k0,k1))
              end
            elif j>=i then
                (j0,j1) = partition(j)
                mma(a,i,b,j0,c,k)
                mma(a,i,b+j0,j1,c,k)
            else
                (i0,i1) = partition(i)
                (mma(a,i0,b,j,c,k),mma(a+i0,i1,b,j,c,k))
            end
        mm(a:ZZ32,i:ZZ32,b:ZZ32,j:ZZ32,c:ZZ32,k:ZZ32):() =
            if k>=i AND k>=j then
              if k=1 then
                res.put((a,c), get(a,b) other.get(b,c))
              else
                (k0,k1) = partition(k)
                (mm(a,i,b,j,c,k0),mm(a,i,b,j,c+k0,k1))
              end
            elif j>=i then
                (j0,j1) = partition(j)
                mm(a,i,b,j0,c,k)
                mma(a,i,b+j0,j1,c,k)
            else
                (i0,i1) = partition(i)
                (mm(a,i0,b,j,c,k),mm(a+i0,i1,b,j,c,k))
            end
        if s0=0 OR s1=0 OR s2=0 then
          res
        else
          mm(0,s0,0,s1,0,s2)
          res
        end
      end
    rmul(v: Vector[\T,s1\]): Vector[\T,s0\] = do
        row(i:ZZ32):T =
            SUM[(j,v_j)<-v.indexValuePairs] get(i,j) v_j
        vector[\T,s0\]().fill(row)
      end
    lmul(v: Vector[\T,s0\]): Vector[\T,s1\] = do
        col(i:ZZ32):T =
            SUM[(j,v_j)<-v.indexValuePairs] v_j get(j,i)
        vector[\T,s1\]().fill(col)
      end
    t(): Matrix[\T,s1,s0\] = TransposedMatrix[\T,s1,s0\](self)
end

(* Default matrix should match default array in column vs row-major. *)
object __DefaultMatrix[\T, nat s0, nat s1\]()
    extends Matrix[\T, s0, s1\]
  mem:PrimitiveArray[\T, (s0 s1) \] = PrimitiveArray[\T, (s0 s1) \]()
  init0(t1:(ZZ32,ZZ32), v:T) : () = do (i,j)=t1; mem.init0(i s1 + j, v) end
  put(t1:(ZZ32,ZZ32), v:T) : () = do (i,j)=t1; mem.put(i s1 + j, v) end
  get(t1:(ZZ32,ZZ32)):T = do (i,j)=t1; mem.get(i s1 + j) end
end

object TransposedMatrix[\T, nat s0, nat s1\](mem:Matrix[\T,s1,s0\])
        extends Matrix[\T, s0, s1\]
    replica[\U\]():Array2[\U,0,s0,0,s1\] = mem.replica[\U\]().t()

    init0(t1:(ZZ32,ZZ32), v:T) : () = do (i,j)=t1; mem.init0((j,i),v) end
    put(t1:(ZZ32,ZZ32), v:T) : () = do (i,j)=t1; mem.put((j,i),v) end
    get(t1:(ZZ32,ZZ32)):T = do (i,j)=t1; mem.get(j,i) end
    t(): Matrix[\T,s1,s0\] = mem
    add(v:TransposedMatrix[\T,s0,s1\]): Matrix[\T,s0,s1\] = mem.add(v.t()).t()
    subtract(v:Matrix[\T,s0,s1\]): Matrix[\T,s0,s1\] = mem.subtract(v.t()).t()
    negate(): Matrix[\T,s0,s1\] = mem.negate().t()
    scale(f: T): Matrix[\T,s0,s1\] = mem.scale(f).t()
    rmul(v: Vector[\T,s1\]): Vector[\T,s0\] = mem.lmul(v)
    lmul(v: Vector[\T,s0\]): Vector[\T,s1\] = mem.rmul(v)
(*  Can't overload generic methods yet, but this is preferable.
    mul[\nat s2\](v:TransposedMatrix[\T,s1,s2\]): Matrix[\T,s0,s2\] =
        v.t().mul(mem).t()
*)
end

__builtinFactory2[\T,nat b0,nat s0,nat b1,nat s1\]():Array2[\T,b0,s0,b1,s1\] =
    if b0=0 AND b1=0 then
        array2[\T,s0,s1\]()
    else
        __DefaultArray2[\T,b0,s0,b1,s1\]()
    end

(* array2 is a factory for 0-based 2-D arrays. *)
(* TODO: fix when Number is covariant. *)
array2[\T, nat s0, nat s1\]():Array2[\T,0,s0,0,s1\] =
    typecase __thrower[\T\] of
        ()->Number => matrix[\T,s0,s1\]()
        else => __DefaultArray2[\T,0,s0,0,s1\]()
    end
array2[\T, nat s0, nat s1\](v:T):Array2[\T,0,s0,0,s1\] =
  array2[\T,s0,s1\]().fill(v)
array2[\T, nat s0, nat s1\](f:(ZZ32,ZZ32)->T):Array2[\T,0,s0,0,s1\] =
  array2[\T,s0,s1\]().fill(f)

(* matrix is the same as array1, but specialized to numeric type
   arguments, except that the default value (if given) is used to
   construct a multiple of the identity matrix. *)
matrix[\T extends Number, nat s0, nat s1\]():Matrix[\T,s0,s1\] =
  __DefaultMatrix[\T,s0,s1\]()
matrix[\T extends Number, nat s0, nat s1\](v:T):Matrix[\T,s0,s1\] =
  array2[\T,s0,s1\]().fill(fn (x:ZZ32,y:ZZ32):T => if x=y then v else 0 end)

(* Matrix multiplication; used to use a cache-oblivious algorithm, but
   we ran into trouble due to lack of support for atomic increment of
   matrix elements. *)
opr DOT[\ T extends Number, nat n, nat m, nat p\]
       (me:Matrix[\T,n,m\], other:Matrix[\T,m,p\]): Matrix[\T,n,p\] =
        me.mul[\p\](other)

opr juxtaposition[\ T extends Number, nat n, nat m, nat p\]
     (me:Matrix[\T,n,m\], other:Matrix[\T,m,p\]): Matrix[\T,n,p\] =
        me.mul[\p\](other)


(* matrix-vector multiplication *)
opr DOT[\ T extends Number, nat n, nat m \]
       (me:Matrix[\T,n,m\], v:Vector[\T,m\]):Vector[\T,n\] = me.rmul(v)

opr juxtaposition[\ T extends Number, nat n, nat m \]
     (me:Matrix[\T,n,m\], v:Vector[\T,m\]):Vector[\T,n\] = me.rmul(v)

(* vector-matrix multiplication *)
opr DOT[\ T extends Number, nat n, nat m \]
       (v:Vector[\T,n\], me:Matrix[\T,n,m\]):Vector[\T,m\] = me.lmul(v)

opr juxtaposition[\ T extends Number, nat n, nat m \]
     (v:Vector[\T,n\], me:Matrix[\T,n,m\]):Vector[\T,m\] = me.lmul(v)

opr DOT[\ T extends Number, nat n, nat m \]
       (me : Matrix[\T,n,m\], other : T) : Matrix[\T,n,m\] = me.scale(other)

opr juxtaposition[\ T extends Number, nat n, nat m \]
     (me : Matrix[\T,n,m\], other : T) : Matrix[\T,n,m\] = me.scale(other)

opr DOT[\ T extends Number, nat n, nat m \]
       (other : T, me : Matrix[\T,n,m\]) : Matrix[\T,n,m\] = me.scale(other)

opr juxtaposition[\ T extends Number, nat n, nat m \]
     (other : T, me : Matrix[\T,n,m\]) : Matrix[\T,n,m\] = me.scale(other)

(** Array3[\T,b0,s0,b1,s1,b2,s2\] is the type of 3-dimensional arrays
    of element type T, with size s_i in the i^th dimension and lowest
    index (b0,b1,b2).  Natural order for all generators in each
    dimension is from b to b+s-1; the overall order of elements need
    only be consistent with the cross product of these orderings (see
    Generator.cross()). **)
trait Array3[\T, nat b0, nat s0, nat b1, nat s1, nat b2, nat s2\]
    extends { Indexed1[\s0\], Indexed2[\s1\], Indexed3[\s2\], Rank3,
              StandardMutableArrayType[\Array3[\T,b0,s0,b1,s1,b2,s2\],T,
                                        (ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\] }
    excludes { Number, String }

    getter size():ZZ32 = s0 s1 s2
    getter sizes():(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32) = (s0, s1, s2)
    getter bounds():CompactFullRange3D[\ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32\] =
        sized3Range[\ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32\](0,0,0,b0,b1,b2,s0,s1,s2)

    getter asString():String = do
      r : String := "[" b0 "#" s0 "," b1 "#" s1 "," b2 "#" s2 "]"
      row(i,k) =
          for j <- seq(0#s1) do
            r := r " " self[b0+i,b1+j,b2+k]
          end
      plane(k) =
        if s1 > 0 then
          row(0,k)
          for i <- seq(1#(s0-1)) do
            r := r // " "
            row(i,k)
          end
        end
      if s0=0 then
        r "[]"
      else
        r := r // "["
        plane(0)
        for k <- seq(1#(s2-1)) do
          r := r " ;;" //  " "
          plane(k)
        end
        r " ]"
      end
    end

    opr |self| : ZZ32 = s0 s1 s2

    (* Again, offset performs bounds checking and shifts to 0 indexing. *)
    offset(t:(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)):(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32) = do
      (a0,a1,a2)=t
      c0 = a0 - b0; c1 = a1 - b1; c2 = a2 - b2
      if NOT (0 <= c0 < s0) then oops(1, b0, s0, a0); end
      if NOT (0 <= c1 < s1) then oops(2, b1, s1, a1); end
      if NOT (0 <= c2 < s2) then oops(3, b2, s2, a2); end
      (c0,c1,c2)
    end
    toIndex(t:(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)):(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32) =
        do (a0,a1,a2) = t; (a0+b0,a1+b1,a2+b2) end

    (* And get and put are 0-indexed without bounds checks. *)
    put(t:(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32), v:T) : ()
    get(t:(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)):T

    opr[i:ZZ32, j:ZZ32, k:ZZ32] := (v:T): () = do self[ (i,j,k) ] := v end
    opr[r:Range[\(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\]]: Array[\T,(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
        r' = self.bounds.narrowToRange(r)
        (z0,z1,z2) = r'.extent.get
        (l0,l1,l2) = r'.left.get (*'*)
        (m0,m1,m2) = r'.stride (*'*)
        __subarray(self, N[\0\],reflect(z0), N[\0\],reflect(z1),
                   N[\0\],reflect(z2), reflect(l0),reflect(l1), reflect(l2),m0,m1,m2)
      end
    opr[_:TrivialOpenRange] : Array3[\T,0,s0,0,s1,0,s2\] =
        subarray[\0,s0,0,s1,0,s2,0,0,0\](1,1,1)
    shift(t:(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)): Array[\T,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
        (o0,o1,o2)=t
        if o0=0 AND o1=0 AND o2=0 then
            self
        else
            __subarray(self,
                       reflect(o0),N[\s0\], reflect(o1),N[\s1\],
                       reflect(o2),N[\s2\], N[\b0\],N[\b1\],N[\b2\],1,1,1)
        end
      end

    (** 3-D subarray given static subarray parameters.
        %(bo0,bo1,bo2)#(so0,so1,so2)% are output bounds.
        The result is the subarray starting at %(o0,o1,o2)% in the original array,
        striding by (m0,m1,m2).
     **)
    subarray[\nat bo0, nat so0, nat bo1, nat so1, nat bo2, nat so2,
              nat o0, nat o1, nat o2\]
            (m0:ZZ32,m1:ZZ32,m2:ZZ32): Array3[\T,bo0,so0,bo1,so1,bo2,so2\] = do
        boundsCheck = self.bounds.narrowToRange( (o0,o1,o2)::(m0,m1,m2)#(so0,so1,so2) )
        SubArray3[\T,bo0,so0,bo1,so1,bo2,so2,b0,s0,b1,s1,b2,s2\](self,m0,o0,m1,o1,m2,o2)
      end

    zeroIndices():CompactFullRange3D[\ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32\] =
        sized3Range[\ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32\](0,0,0,0,0,0,s0,s1,s2)

    replica[\U\]():Array3[\U,b0,s0,b1,s1,b2,s2\] =
        __DefaultArray3[\U,b0,s0,b1,s1,b2,s2\]()
    copy():Array3[\T,b0,s0,b1,s1,b2,s2\] =
        self.replica[\T\]().fill(fn (i:ZZ32,j:ZZ32,k:ZZ32):T =>
                                     get(i-b0,j-b1,k-b2))
    map[\R\](f:T->R): Array3[\R,b0,s0,b1,s1,b2,s2\] =
        replica[\R\]().fill(fn (i:ZZ32,j:ZZ32,k:ZZ32):R =>
                                f(get(i-b0,j-b1,k-b2)))

    of element type T, with size s_i in the i^th dimension and lowest

    dimension is from b to b+s-1; the overall order of elements need
    only be consistent with the cross product of these orderings (see
    Generator.cross()). **)

    extends { Indexed1[\s0\], Indexed2[\s1\], Indexed3[\s2\], Rank3,

                                        (ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\] }
    excludes { Number, String }

    getter size():ZZ32 = s0 s1 s2
    getter sizes():(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32) = (s0, s1, s2)
    getter bounds():CompactFullRange3D[\ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32\] =
        sized3Range[\ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32\](0,0,0,b0,b1,b2,s0,s1,s2)

    getter asString():String = do
      r : String := "[" b0 "#" s0 "," b1 "#" s1 "," b2 "#" s2 "]"
      row(i,k) =
          for j <- seq(0#s1) do
            r := r " " self[b0+i,b1+j,b2+k]
          end
      plane(k) =
        if s1 > 0 then
          row(0,k)
          for i <- seq(1#(s0-1)) do
            r := r // " "
            row(i,k)
          end
        end
      if s0=0 then
        r "[]"
      else
        r := r // "["
        plane(0)
        for k <- seq(1#(s2-1)) do
          r := r " ;;" //  " "
          plane(k)
        end
        r " ]"
      end
    end

    opr |self| : ZZ32 = s0 s1 s2

    (* Again, offset performs bounds checking and shifts to 0 indexing. *)
    offset(t:(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)):(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32) = do
      (a0,a1,a2)=t

      if NOT (0 <= c1 < s1) then oops(2, b1, s1, a1); end

    end

        do (a0,a1,a2) = t; (a0+b0,a1+b1,a2+b2) end

trait Array[\E,I\] extends { ReadableArray[\E,I\], MutableIndexed[\E,I\] }
    (** 0-based non-bounds-checked indexing **)
    put(i:I, e:E): ()
    opr[i:I]:=(v:E):() = put(offset(i),v)

    opr[r:Range[\I\]]:=(a:Indexed[\E,I\]):() = do
        a0 = a[#]        (* Make a have 0 origin *)
        s0 = self[r]            (* Make self have 0 origin *)
        if a0.bounds = s0.bounds then
            for (i,v) <- a0.indexValuePairs do
                s0.put(i,v)
            end
        else
            fail("Can't assign indexed with bounds " a.bounds //
                 " to differently-sized subarray " s0.bounds)
        end
      end

    (** The following are repetition with better return type info. **)
    opr[r:Range[\I\]] : Array[\E,I\]
    opr[_:TrivialOpenRange] : Array[\E,I\]
    ivmap[\R\](f:(I,E)->R): Array[\R, I\]

api NatReflect

(** Reflection for run-time integers into compile-time nat parameters.
 *
 *  Basically you can call the function reflect(n) and it will return
 *  an instance of NatParam.  But every instance of NatParam is an
 *  object N[\n\], so we can write a function which takes N[\n\] and
 *  pass it a NatParam; within that function n becomes a static nat
 *  parameter.
 *)
trait NatParam
  (* comprises { N[\n\] } where [\ nat n \] *)
  abstract getter toZZ() : ZZ32
end

end

(* Actually convert a ZZ32 into a NatParam. *)
reflect(z:ZZ32):NatParam

end

content.content:
---- readme
5:The question is not whether APL can be written in Fortress but how far the specification's syntax-extension mechanism and the library carry it before something gives, and what exactly gives. The method is the one the microGPT work settled on: each step is bounded, every probe is kept with its output, every negative claim is gated by an attempt to achieve the thing, and every new language fact goes into `gaps.md` here in the merged ledger's row format for a later merge.
7:The rungs follow the chapters of Stefan Kruger's "Learning APL" (https://xpqz.github.io/learnapl/), read in order; the reader climbs by reading the chapter, the exploration climbs by making that chapter's examples run inside `apl⦇ … ⦈` and agree with the book's printed results or with an oracle. One directory per rung.
9:| rung | chapter | what it needs from Fortress | state |
11:| 1 | It's arrays all the way down (`array.html`) | arrays, strands, scalar extension, `⍳ ⍴`, reductions, rank | done twice: 26 of 26 checks over 18 of 28 examples pass on the **native-array base**, 10 out of scope (nested arrays, `]box`, `⎕` names), plus 18 of 18 beyond the chapter; `rung-1/REPORT.md` prices that base against v1's and keeps the 21 probes `r01`-`r16` behind it. The first run, on v1's runtime-rank library, is `v1-probes/ (the probes and reports of the retired first library, kept because gap rows cite them; the library itself is in git history only)` |
12:| 2 | Indexing (`indexing.html`) | bracket indexing, `⌷`, index origin | done twice: 25 of 25 checks over 19 of the 40 examples pass on the native-array base (the goldens call only 5 "core"), same 19 and same 25 as v1, nothing regressed; 21 out of scope (16 nested `m`, `⎕`/`]`, tacit `⌷⍨∘⊃⍨⍤`, characters); 21 of 21 beyond the chapter. APL names are now **lambda parameters**, assignment is an **in-place put** on the library's own mutable arrays, and a row or column is a **view that is a `Vector`**; `rung-2/REPORT.md`. The workspace-table version is `v1/rung-2/`, the variables-only study `v1/rung-2b/` |
13:| 2b | Indexing again, variables only | APL names as **real Fortress variables** | done: the lambda route of the paper's design works — an `Id` gap as a lambda parameter binds, the name needs no `⍎(…)` escape, and host code in the block reads it; 52 of 52 checks, the chapter's variable examples run both by lambda binding and over host-declared cells, which also recovers rebinding and the cross-block session; costs a closed name set (1 grammar line per name) because a reference cannot be a gap. Also: what the shipped `Regex.fsi` teaches about delimiting, `#` and escaping, and a newline-terminated `apl 2 3 ⍴ ⍳ 6` form. `v1/rung-2b/REPORT.md`. Carried over to rung 2 on the new base, minus the cell — the library's arrays are mutable, so assignment needs no rebinding (`gaps.md` row 48) |
14:| 3 | Glyphiary (`manip.html`) | the bulk of the primitives, monadic and dyadic | done: 43 of 43 checks over 29 of the chapter's 59 examples pass on the native-array base, 30 out of scope (17 nested, 9 characters, `⍤` and the bracket axis, dfns, a tacit definition, a run-time reshape shape), plus 31 of 31 beyond the chapter — the microGPT overloads: matrix arithmetic with scalar extension, comparisons on matrices, monadic `*`, `⍟`, `(a,b)⍴x`, take and drop on two axes, `⍨`. The library grew by 143 declarations over six private zips, the grammar by 77 alternatives. The new mechanism is the **glyph as a value**: a nonterminal of 31 untyped host lambdas, which still dispatch on rank at the call, so `⍨` is two rules and rungs 4-6 inherit the shape for `/ ¨ ⍤ ∘.` and `.`; `rung-3/REPORT.md` keeps the eight probes behind it |
15:| 4 | Direct functions and operators (`functions.html`) | `{⍵}` dfns as generated `fn`, user operators | done: 18 of 18 checks over 14 of the chapter's 29 examples pass, 15 out of scope (`⎕ ]`, characters, modified assignment, a local re-binding an enclosing name, n-wise reduction, tacit, dops `⍺⍺`), plus 31 of 31 beyond the chapter — rank 3 end to end, the rank operator `⍤1 ⍤2` in both valences, `0∘⌈`, `⊢ ⊣`, `∇` recursion, guards, `softmax` and `rmsnorm`. The rung's mechanism is the **frame stack**: every APL function value, glyphs included, is a zero-parameter lambda and `⍺ ⍵ ∇` are reads of the top frame, which is the only shape that survives nesting (the host refuses every nested re-declaration of a name) and costs 3.5× a direct `+` on scalars and nothing measurable on 100-element vectors. Its one blocked road was a result type: an overloaded function declared to return `Any` does not dispatch at all (`gaps.md` row 67), so the rank operator returns `Object`. `rung-4/REPORT.md` keeps the 21 probes `u01`-`u21` behind it |
16:| 5 | Iteration (`iteration.html`) | `¨`, power operator, recursion | done: 23 of 23 checks over 14 of the chapter's 40 examples pass, 26 out of scope (nested arrays, `?` Deal, `⎕ ]`, characters, bracket axis, n-wise reduction, dops `⍺⍺ ⍵⍵`, set assignment `⊢←`, `cmpx`), plus 21 of 21 beyond the chapter — each over a strand of three matrices, destructuring, power with a count and with a stop condition, the five scans on both axes, a dfn as the operand of `/ ⌿ \`. The rung's mechanism is the **tuple**: APL's strand of arrays `wq wk wv` is a Fortress tuple and `Q K Vv ← e` is a lambda of three parameters applied to it, so no nested array is ever built. Its one blocked road was the strand over ordinary names — a line break does not separate two names either (`gaps.md` row 81), so a strand reads a **third** closed name set. `rung-5/REPORT.md` keeps the seven probes `v01`-`v07` behind it |
17:| 6 | Products (`products.html`) | inner and outer products `+.×`, `∘.×` | done: 16 of 16 checks over 12 of the chapter's 18 examples pass, 6 out of scope (`⎕ ]`, characters, tacit `prod ← ∘.×`, the `X` operator `⍺⍺` and `⎕CR`), plus 17 of 17 beyond the chapter — the program's attention score `(Qh+.×⍤2⊢⍉⍤2⊢Kh)÷Hd*0.5` over rank 3, `ids∘.=⍳Vs` as a one-hot and `(⍉ids∘.=⍳Vs)+.×dX` as a scatter-add, the causal mask, `vm ×⍤0 1⊢Pr` and `tg⌷⍤0 1⊢Pr`. The rung's mechanism is **a product the library already had**: the shipped `opr DOT` does the inner product in all four rank pairs on runtime-built arrays, 1.46× a hand-written loop, so `aplMatMul` is `DOT` with a LENGTH ERROR contract above it. The direct `+.×` rule costs **3.8×** less than the general `{⍺+⍵}.{⍺×⍵}` on a 16×16 product (`gaps.md` row 85), which is the whole argument for the direct rules of rungs 1, 3, 5 and 6. `rung-6/REPORT.md` keeps the four probes `w01`-`w04` behind it |
23:Layout: `base/` holds the library and grammar the rungs share (`AplCore.fss` with its API, `AplSyntax.fsi` with the grammar), grown rung by rung; `rung-N/` holds that rung's examples as a Fortress component, its expected results, its probes with outputs, and a short `REPORT.md`; `goldens/` holds the book's examples with their printed results per chapter, and the oracle's results where an oracle exists; `gaps.md` is the running gap table.
25:The base was **replaced once**, on 2026-09-13. The first library (rungs 1, 2 and 2b) carried one `value object AplArr(shape, data)` with the rank as run-time data and dispatched every primitive on a string; it was an interpreter nested inside the interpreter and taught nothing about Fortress, so it was retired on 2026-09-13 (git history before 0ff5eae27); only its probes and reports remain, under `v1-probes/`, because rows 1-35 of `gaps.md` cite them and those findings about the extension mechanism stand. The base now is the **native-array** design: an APL scalar is an `RR64`, a vector an `Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]`, a matrix an `Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]`, rank lives in the type, each glyph is a real Fortress operator in both arities where the host's operator table allows one, the templates expand to host code, and `SUM`/`PROD`/`BIG MAX` and `requires` contracts come from the library rather than from us. It was priced against v1 before being promoted (`rung-1/REPORT.md`).

mmSum[\nat n, nat m, nat p\](a: Matrix[\RR64,n,m\], b: Matrix[\RR64,m,p\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do

mmLoop[\nat n, nat m, nat p\](a: Matrix[\RR64,n,m\], b: Matrix[\RR64,m,p\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do

    (br, bc) = b.sizes

cat > explorations/run-c/src/MicroGptFlat.fss <<'EOF'
(* MicroGptFlat -- microGPT in native Fortress arrays, data designed after Hsu.
   Reference: explorations/apl/reference/hsu-flat/microgpt_concise.dyalog,
   followed line for line; the design notes are explorations/run-c/design.md.
   Run from explorations/run-c/src (the corpus and weight paths are relative). *)
component MicroGptFlat
export MicroGptFlat
export Executable
import NatReflect.{...}
import File.{...}
import System.{...}

(* --------------------------------------------------- hyperparameters ---- *)
nEmbd: ZZ32 = 16
blockSize: ZZ32 = 16
nHead: ZZ32 = 4
headDim: ZZ32 = 4
vocabSize: ZZ32 = 27
bosId: ZZ32 = 26
epsRms: RR64 = 10.0^(-5)
lr0: RR64 = 0.01
beta1: RR64 = 0.85
beta2: RR64 = 0.99
epsAdam: RR64 = 10.0^(-8)
scheduleLength: ZZ32 = 1000

corpusPath: String = "../../apl/reference/dzaima/docs.txt"
weightsDir: String = "../../apl/reference/dzaima/w"

(* --------------------------------------------- array constructors ------- *)
vec(n: ZZ32, f: ZZ32 -> RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = array[\RR64\](n).fill(f)
zeros(n: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = array[\RR64\](n).fill(0.0)
keys(n: ZZ32, f: ZZ32 -> ZZ32): Array[\ZZ32,ZZ32\] = array[\ZZ32\](n).fill(f)
mat(r: ZZ32, c: ZZ32, f: (ZZ32,ZZ32) -> RR64): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = array[\RR64\](r,c).fill(f)
zerosM(r: ZZ32, c: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = array[\RR64\](r,c).fill(0.0)

(* --------------------------------- tactic 2/8: one vector, nine views --- *)
matName(i: ZZ32): String =
    if i = 0 then "wte" elif i = 1 then "wpe" elif i = 2 then "lm_head"
    elif i = 3 then "attn_wq" elif i = 4 then "attn_wk" elif i = 5 then "attn_wv"
    elif i = 6 then "attn_wo" elif i = 7 then "mlp_fc1" else "mlp_fc2" end
matRows(i: ZZ32): ZZ32 = if (i = 0) OR (i = 2) then vocabSize elif i = 7 then 4 nEmbd else nEmbd end
matCols(i: ZZ32): ZZ32 = if i = 8 then 4 nEmbd else nEmbd end
matCount(i: ZZ32): ZZ32 = matRows(i) matCols(i)
matOffset(i: ZZ32): ZZ32 = SUM[j <- 0#i] matCount(j)
nParams(): ZZ32 = SUM[j <- 0#9] matCount(j)

(* matrix i as a zero-copy view of the flat vector: rows x cols at off, row-major *)
object PView[\nat s, nat r, nat c\](base: Vector[\RR64,s\], off: ZZ32)
        extends Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]
    get(ij:(ZZ32,ZZ32)): RR64 = do (i,j) = ij; base.get(off + i c + j) end
    put(ij:(ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = do (i,j) = ij; base.put(off + i c + j, x) end
    init0(ij:(ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = do (i,j) = ij; base.init0(off + i c + j, x) end
    replica[\U\](): Array2[\U,0,r,0,c\] = array2[\U,r,c\]()
end
viewOf[\nat s, nat r, nat c\](base: Vector[\RR64,s\], off: ZZ32, _: N[\r\], _: N[\c\]): Matrix[\RR64,r,c\] =
    PView[\s,r,c\](base, off)
view[\nat s\](p: Vector[\RR64,s\], i: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    viewOf(p, matOffset(i), reflect(matRows(i)), reflect(matCols(i)))

(* a (rows x cols) block of a matrix at (r0, c0): the per-document, per-head
   slice of a (doc.pos x 16) activation, zero-copy, readable and writable *)
object Block[\nat br, nat bc, nat r, nat c\](base: Matrix[\RR64,br,bc\], r0: ZZ32, c0: ZZ32)
        extends Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]
    get(ij:(ZZ32,ZZ32)): RR64 = do (i,j) = ij; base.get(r0 + i, c0 + j) end
    put(ij:(ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = do (i,j) = ij; base.put((r0 + i, c0 + j), x) end
    init0(ij:(ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = do (i,j) = ij; base.init0((r0 + i, c0 + j), x) end
    replica[\U\](): Array2[\U,0,r,0,c\] = array2[\U,r,c\]()
end
blockOf[\nat br, nat bc, nat r, nat c\](base: Matrix[\RR64,br,bc\], r0: ZZ32, c0: ZZ32, _: N[\r\], _: N[\c\]): Matrix[\RR64,r,c\] =
    Block[\br,bc,r,c\](base, r0, c0)
block[\nat br, nat bc\](base: Matrix[\RR64,br,bc\], r0: ZZ32, c0: ZZ32, rows: ZZ32, cols: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    blockOf(base, r0, c0, reflect(rows), reflect(cols))
(* head h of document d in a (doc.pos x 16) activation, and head-cell (d,h) of
   the stacked attention matrices *)
head[\nat br, nat bc\](a: Matrix[\RR64,br,bc\], d: ZZ32, h: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    block(a, d blockSize, h headDim, blockSize, headDim)
headCell[\nat br, nat bc\](a: Matrix[\RR64,br,bc\], d: ZZ32, h: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    block(a, (d nHead + h) blockSize, 0, blockSize, blockSize)
assignInto[\nat r, nat c, nat p, nat q\](dest: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], src: Matrix[\RR64,p,q\]): () = do
    dest.assign(fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => src[i,j])
  end

(* ------------------------------------------------ the array vocabulary -- *)
opr (m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\])^T[\nat r, nat c\]: Matrix[\RR64,c,r\] = m.t()
opr /[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], s: RR64): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    mat(rows, cols, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => m[i,j] / s)
  end
opr /[\nat n\](a: Vector[\RR64,n\], b: Vector[\RR64,n\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = vec(|a|, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => a[i] / b[i])
opr /[\nat n\](a: Vector[\RR64,n\], s: RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = vec(|a|, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => a[i] / s)
opr +[\nat n\](a: Vector[\RR64,n\], s: RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = vec(|a|, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => a[i] + s)
opr SQRT[\nat n\](a: Vector[\RR64,n\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = vec(|a|, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => SQRT (a[i]))

(* rows of m at the keys: wte[ids;] *)
gather[\nat r, nat c, nat k\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], ks: Vector[\ZZ32,k\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    mat(|ks|, cols, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => m[ks[i], j])
  end
(* tactic 10: keys -> one-hot: ids∘.=⍳VS *)
onehot[\nat k\](ks: Vector[\ZZ32,k\], width: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    mat(|ks|, width, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => if ks[i] = j then 1.0 else 0.0 end)
(* row i of m times v[i]: v ×⍤0 1⊢m *)
scaleRows[\nat n, nat r, nat c\](v: Vector[\RR64,n\], m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    mat(rows, cols, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => v[i] m[i,j])
  end
hadamard[\nat r, nat c, nat p, nat q\](a: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], b: Matrix[\RR64,p,q\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (rows, cols) = a.sizes
    mat(rows, cols, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => a[i,j] b[i,j])
  end
relu[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    m.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => 0.0 MAX x)
positive[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    m.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => if x > 0.0 then 1.0 else 0.0 end)

(* rmsn⍤1: each row divided by sqrt(mean of squares + eps) *)
rmsnRows[\nat r, nat c\](x: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (n, d) = x.sizes
    rr = vec(n, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => SQRT ((SUM[j <- 0#d] (x[i,j])^2) / d + epsRms))
    mat(n, d, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => x[i,j] / rr[i])
  end
(* dy rmsn_b x: with y = x/r, (dy - y mean(y dy)) / r *)
rmsnRowsB[\nat r, nat c, nat p, nat q\](dy: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], x: Matrix[\RR64,p,q\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (n, d) = x.sizes
    rr = vec(n, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => SQRT ((SUM[j <- 0#d] (x[i,j])^2) / d + epsRms))
    y = mat(n, d, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => x[i,j] / rr[i])
    yd = vec(n, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => (SUM[j <- 0#d] y[i,j] dy[i,j]) / d)
    mat(n, d, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => (dy[i,j] - y[i,j] yd[i]) / rr[i])
  end
(* sm⍤1: softmax of each row *)
smRows[\nat r, nat c\](z: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (n, d) = z.sizes
    mx = vec(n, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => BIG MAX[j <- 0#d] z[i,j])
    e = mat(n, d, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => exp(z[i,j] - mx[i]))
    sums = vec(n, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => SUM[j <- 0#d] e[i,j])
    mat(n, d, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => e[i,j] / sums[i])
  end
(* p sm_b dy: p (dy - sum(p dy)) per row *)
smRowsB[\nat r, nat c, nat p, nat q\](pm: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], dy: Matrix[\RR64,p,q\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (n, d) = pm.sizes
    pd = vec(n, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => SUM[j <- 0#d] pm[i,j] dy[i,j])
    mat(n, d, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => pm[i,j] (dy[i,j] - pd[i]))
  end
(* tactic 9: the causal mask as an additive matrix, ¯1E10 above the diagonal *)
causalMask: Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    mat(blockSize, blockSize, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => if j > i then -(10.0^10) else 0.0 end)

(* --------------------------------------------------- the loaders -------- *)
(* decimal digits, optional '.', optional e/E exponent; leading '-' or '¯' *)
parseFloat(s: String): RR64 = do
    neg = (s[0] = '-') OR (s[0] = '¯')
    m: RR64 := 0.0
    scale: ZZ32 := 0
    ex: ZZ32 := 0
    i: ZZ32 := if neg then 1 else 0 end
    seenPoint: Boolean := false
    n = |s|
    while (i < n) AND: ((s[i] =/= 'e') AND (s[i] =/= 'E')) do
        c = s[i]
        if c = '.' then seenPoint := true
        else
            m := 10.0 m + (c.codePoint - '0'.codePoint)
            if seenPoint then scale += 1 end
        end
        i += 1
    end
    if i < n then ex := strToInt(s[(i+1) # (n - i - 1)]) end
    e10 = ex - scale
    r = if e10 >= 0 then m (10.0^e10)
        elif e10 >= -22 then m / (10.0^(-e10))
        else (m / (10.0^22)) / (10.0^(-e10 - 22)) end
    if neg then -r else r end
  end
(* every space-separated number on a line goes to out[off..]; returns the count *)
parseRow[\nat s\](line: String, out: Vector[\RR64,s\], off: ZZ32): ZZ32 = do
    n = |line|
    i: ZZ32 := 0
    k: ZZ32 := 0
    while i < n do
        if line[i] = ' ' then i += 1
        else
            j: ZZ32 := i
            while (j < n) AND: (line[j] =/= ' ') do j += 1 end
            out[off + k] := parseFloat(line[i # (j - i)])
            k += 1
            i := j
        end
    end
    k
  end
(* the nine text files, one row per line, straight into the flat vector *)
loadParams(dir: String): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do
    p = zeros(nParams())
    for i <- seq(0#9) do
        f = FileReadStream(dir "/" matName(i) ".txt")
        for r <- seq(0#matRows(i)) do
            k = parseRow(f.readLine(), p, matOffset(i) + r matCols(i))
            if k =/= matCols(i) then fail("row " r " of " matName(i) " has " k " numbers, expected " matCols(i)) end
        end
        f.close()
    end
    p
  end

(* tactic 3/5: the corpus as one padded integer matrix (docs x 17), BOS before
   and after each name and in every unused slot, plus a length per document *)
countLines(path: String): ZZ32 = do
    f = FileReadStream(path)
    n: ZZ32 := 0
    line: String := f.readLine()
    while |line| > 0 do n += 1; line := f.readLine() end
    f.close()
    n
  end
loadCorpus(path: String): (Array[\ZZ32,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\], Array[\ZZ32,ZZ32\]) = do
    nd = countLines(path)
    tokm = array[\ZZ32\](nd, blockSize + 1).fill(bosId)
    len = array[\ZZ32\](nd).fill(0)
    f = FileReadStream(path)
    for d <- seq(0#nd) do
        name = f.readLine()
        for j <- seq(0#|name|) do tokm[d, 1 + j] := name[j].codePoint - 'a'.codePoint end
        len[d] := 1 + |name|
    end
    f.close()
    (tokm, len)
  end
(corpusTokens, corpusLengths) = loadCorpus(corpusPath)
nDocs(): ZZ32 = |corpusLengths|
docLength(d: ZZ32): ZZ32 = corpusLengths[d]
tokenAt(d: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): ZZ32 = corpusTokens[d, j]

(* ------------------------- the step: keys -> (loss, flat gradient). Pure. -- *)
step(p: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], b: Array[\ZZ32,ZZ32\]): (RR64, Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]) = do
    bsz = |b|
    n = bsz blockSize
    ids = keys(n, fn (r: ZZ32): ZZ32 => corpusTokens[b[r DIV blockSize], r MOD blockSize])
    tg = keys(n, fn (r: ZZ32): ZZ32 => corpusTokens[b[r DIV blockSize], (r MOD blockSize) + 1])
    vm = vec(n, fn (r: ZZ32): RR64 => if (r MOD blockSize) < corpusLengths[b[r DIV blockSize]] then 1.0 else 0.0 end)
    nv = SUM[r <- 0#n] vm[r]
    pos = keys(n, fn (r: ZZ32): ZZ32 => r MOD blockSize)
    wte = view(p, 0); wpe = view(p, 1); lm = view(p, 2)
    wq = view(p, 3); wk = view(p, 4); wv = view(p, 5); wo = view(p, 6)
    f1 = view(p, 7); f2 = view(p, 8)
    (* -- forward, all (doc,pos) rows at once -- *)
    x = gather(wte, ids) + gather(wpe, pos)
    xp = rmsnRows(x); x1 = rmsnRows(xp)
    q = x1 (wq^T); kk = x1 (wk^T); vv = x1 (wv^T)
    att = zerosM(bsz nHead blockSize, blockSize)
    hc = zerosM(n, nEmbd)
    for d <- 0#bsz, h <- 0#nHead do
        qh = head(q, d, h); kh = head(kk, d, h); vh = head(vv, d, h)
        ah = headCell(att, d, h)
        assignInto(ah, smRows((qh (kh^T)) / (SQRT (1.0 headDim)) + causalMask))
        assignInto(head(hc, d, h), ah vh)
    end
    x2 = xp + hc (wo^T)
    x3 = rmsnRows(x2); m0 = x3 (f1^T); mr = relu(m0)
    x4 = x2 + mr (f2^T)
    pr = smRows(x4 (lm^T))
    loss = -(SUM[r <- 0#n] vm[r] (log(pr[r, tg[r]]))) / nv
    (* -- backward, one line under each forward line, bottom-up -- *)
    g = zeros(nParams())
    dL = scaleRows(vm / nv, pr - onehot(tg, vocabSize))
    assignInto(view(g, 2), (dL^T) x4); dX4 = dL lm
    assignInto(view(g, 8), (dX4^T) mr); dM0 = hadamard(dX4 f2, positive(m0))
    assignInto(view(g, 7), (dM0^T) x3); dX3 = dM0 f1
    dX2 = dX4 + rmsnRowsB(dX3, x2)
    assignInto(view(g, 6), (dX2^T) hc); dH = dX2 wo
    dQ = zerosM(n, nEmbd); dK = zerosM(n, nEmbd); dV = zerosM(n, nEmbd)
    for d <- 0#bsz, h <- 0#nHead do
        ah = headCell(att, d, h); dh = head(dH, d, h)
        qh = head(q, d, h); kh = head(kk, d, h); vh = head(vv, d, h)
        assignInto(head(dV, d, h), (ah^T) dh)
        dS = smRowsB(ah, dh (vh^T)) / (SQRT (1.0 headDim))
        assignInto(head(dQ, d, h), dS kh)
        assignInto(head(dK, d, h), (dS^T) qh)
    end
    assignInto(view(g, 3), (dQ^T) x1); assignInto(view(g, 4), (dK^T) x1); assignInto(view(g, 5), (dV^T) x1)
    dX1 = dQ wq + dK wk + dV wv
    dXp = dX2 + rmsnRowsB(dX1, xp); dX = rmsnRowsB(dXp, x)
    assignInto(view(g, 0), (onehot(ids, vocabSize)^T) dX)
    assignInto(view(g, 1), (onehot(pos, blockSize)^T) dX)
    (loss, g)
  end

(* --------------------- Adam: three whole-vector expressions over P, M, V -- *)
adam(p: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], m: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], v: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\],
     g: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], tstep: ZZ32, lr: RR64):
    (Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]) = do
    m' = beta1 m + (1 - beta1) g
    v' = beta2 v + (1 - beta2) (g.pmul(g))
    p' = p - (lr (m' / (1 - beta1^tstep))) / ((SQRT (v' / (1 - beta2^tstep))) + epsAdam)
    (p', m', v')
  end
learningRate(s: ZZ32): RR64 = lr0 (1 - (1.0 s) / scheduleLength)

(* --------------------------------------------------- training ----------- *)
run(): () = do
    println "microgpt flat | params " nParams() " | corpus " nDocs() " x " (blockSize + 1) " | batch 1, 5 steps"
    bsz = 1
    p: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] := loadParams(weightsDir)
    m: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] := zeros(nParams())
    v: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] := zeros(nParams())
    for s <- seq(0#5) do
        b = keys(bsz, fn (i: ZZ32): ZZ32 => (s bsz + i) MOD nDocs())
        t0 = nanoTime()
        (l, g) = step(p, b)
        (p, m, v) := adam(p, m, v, g, s + 1, learningRate(s))
        println "step " (s + 1) " loss " l "  (" ((nanoTime() - t0) DIV 1000000) " ms)"
    end
  end
end
EOF

+head[\nat br, nat bc\](a: Matrix[\RR64,br,bc\], d: ZZ32, h: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =

+    yd = vec(n, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => (SUM[j <- 0#d] y[i,j] dy[i,j]) / d)

+    wq = view(p, 3); wk = view(p, 4); wv = view(p, 5); wo = view(p, 6)

(* MicroGptFlatCheck -- the standard of success for Run C, one line per check
   with the measured difference and PASS or FAIL, against the goldens in
   explorations/run-c/goldens (extracted from experiment/run-c-goldens/goldens.json).
   Run from explorations/run-c/src:  ../../../bin/fortress MicroGptFlatCheck.fss *)
component MicroGptFlatCheck
export Executable
import MicroGptFlat.{...}
import File.{...}
import System.{...}

goldensDir: String = "../goldens"
tolLoss: RR64 = 10.0^(-12)
tolGrad: RR64 = 10.0^(-12)
tolFd: RR64 = 10.0^(-8)

(* Python repr floats, one per line *)
parseNum(s: String): RR64 = do
    neg = (s[0] = '-') OR (s[0] = '¯')
    m: RR64 := 0.0
    scale: ZZ32 := 0
    ex: ZZ32 := 0
    i: ZZ32 := if neg then 1 else 0 end
    seenPoint: Boolean := false
    n = |s|
    while (i < n) AND: ((s[i] =/= 'e') AND (s[i] =/= 'E')) do
        c = s[i]
        if c = '.' then seenPoint := true
        else
            m := 10.0 m + (c.codePoint - '0'.codePoint)
            if seenPoint then scale += 1 end
        end
        i += 1
    end
    if i < n then
        eneg = (s[i+1] = '-') OR (s[i+1] = '¯')
        j = if eneg OR (s[i+1] = '+') then i + 2 else i + 1 end
        ex := strToInt(s[j # (n - j)])
        if eneg then ex := -ex end
    end
    e10 = ex - scale
    r = if e10 >= 0 then m (10.0^e10)
        elif e10 >= -22 then m / (10.0^(-e10))
        else (m / (10.0^22)) / (10.0^(-e10 - 22)) end
    if neg then -r else r end
  end
(* the tokens of a line, as numbers *)
numbersOf(line: String): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do
    n = |line|
    cnt: ZZ32 := 0
    i: ZZ32 := 0
    while i < n do
        if line[i] = ' ' then i += 1
        else
            cnt += 1
            while (i < n) AND: (line[i] =/= ' ') do i += 1 end
        end
    end
    out = zeros(cnt)
    k: ZZ32 := 0
    i := 0
    while i < n do
        if line[i] = ' ' then i += 1
        else
            j: ZZ32 := i
            while (j < n) AND: (line[j] =/= ' ') do j += 1 end
            out[k] := parseNum(line[i # (j - i)])
            k += 1
            i := j
        end
    end
    out
  end
readVector(path: String, n: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do
    f = FileReadStream(path)
    v = zeros(n)
    for i <- seq(0#n) do v[i] := parseNum(f.readLine()) end
    f.close()
    v
  end
readLines(path: String): Array[\String,ZZ32\] = do
    f = FileReadStream(path)
    cnt: ZZ32 := 0
    line: String := f.readLine()
    while |line| > 0 do cnt += 1; line := f.readLine() end
    f.close()
    g = FileReadStream(path)
    out = array[\String\](cnt).fill("")
    for i <- seq(0#cnt) do out[i] := g.readLine() end
    g.close()
    out
  end

maxAbsDiff[\nat n, nat m\](a: Vector[\RR64,n\], b: Vector[\RR64,m\]): RR64 =
    BIG MAX[i <- 0#|a|] |a[i] - b[i]|
report(name: String, diff: RR64, tol: RR64): () =
    println name ": diff " diff " " (if diff <= tol then "PASS" else "FAIL" end)

run(): () = do
    println "MicroGptFlat checks | threads " (getProperty("fortress.threads", "?")) " | tolerances: loss " tolLoss " grad " tolGrad " fd " tolFd
    wall0 = nanoTime()
    p0 = loadParams("../../apl/reference/dzaima/w")
    (* 0. the loaders against the goldens' P0 and corpus rows *)
    report("loader: max |P - P0| over 4192", maxAbsDiff(p0, readVector(goldensDir "/P0.txt", 4192)), 0.0)
    rows = readLines(goldensDir "/corpus_first16.txt")
    corpusDiff = BIG MAX[d <- 0#16] do
        nums = numbersOf(rows[d])           (* name len t0 .. t16 : the name is not a number, skip it *)
        BIG MAX[j <- 0#17] |nums[2 + j] - (1.0 tokenAt(d, j))| MAX |nums[1] - (1.0 docLength(d))|
      end
    report("corpus: max |row - golden| over documents 0..15", corpusDiff, 0.0)
    (* 1. batch 1, five Adam steps from the committed weights on documents 0..4 *)
    losses = readVector(goldensDir "/losses_batch1_5steps.txt", 5)
    p: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] := p0
    m: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] := zeros(nParams())
    v: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] := zeros(nParams())
    g0 = zeros(nParams())
    for s <- seq(0#5) do
        b = keys(1, fn (i: ZZ32): ZZ32 => s)
        t0 = nanoTime()
        (l, g) = step(p, b)
        if s = 0 then g0.assign(fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => g[i]) end
        (p, m, v) := adam(p, m, v, g, s + 1, learningRate(s))
        if s = 0 then
            report("step 0 batch 1: max |gradient - golden| over 4192", maxAbsDiff(g0, readVector(goldensDir "/grad_step0.txt", 4192)), tolGrad)
            report("step 0 batch 1: max |P after Adam - golden| over 4192", maxAbsDiff(p, readVector(goldensDir "/P_after_adam.txt", 4192)), tolGrad)
            zeroCount = SUM[i <- 0#nParams()] (if g0[i] = 0.0 then 1 else 0 end)
            report("step 0 batch 1: zero gradient entries - 464", |1.0 zeroCount - 464.0|, 0.0)
        end
        report("batch 1 step " (s + 1) " loss " l " vs " losses[s] " (" ((nanoTime() - t0) DIV 1000000) " ms)", |l - losses[s]|, tolLoss)
    end
    (* 2. batch 4 on documents 0..3 from the initial weights *)
    b4 = readVector(goldensDir "/batch4.txt", 9)      (* loss, 4 single losses, 4 lengths *)
    t4 = nanoTime()
    (l4, g4) = step(p0, keys(4, fn (i: ZZ32): ZZ32 => i))
    report("batch 4 loss " l4 " vs golden " b4[0] " (" ((nanoTime() - t4) DIV 1000000) " ms)", |l4 - b4[0]|, tolLoss)
    singles = zeros(4)
    for d <- seq(0#4) do
        (ld, gd) = step(p0, keys(1, fn (i: ZZ32): ZZ32 => d))
        singles[d] := ld
    end
    weighted = (SUM[d <- 0#4] singles[d] (1.0 docLength(d))) / (SUM[d <- 0#4] 1.0 docLength(d))
    report("batch 4 loss vs token-weighted mean of single-document losses " weighted, |l4 - weighted|, tolLoss)
    (* 3. finite differences at the eleven golden indices, central, eps 1e-6 *)
    eps = 10.0^(-6)
    checkFd(label: String, path: String, bk: Array[\ZZ32,ZZ32\], g: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]): () = do
        fdRows = readLines(path)
        worst: RR64 := 0.0
        for r <- seq(0#|fdRows|) do
            nums = numbersOf(fdRows[r])
            idx = strToInt("" (|\ nums[0] /|))
            pp = p0.copy(); pp[idx] := p0[idx] + eps
            pm = p0.copy(); pm[idx] := p0[idx] - eps
            (lp, gp) = step(pp, bk)
            (lm, gm) = step(pm, bk)
            fd = (lp - lm) / (2 eps)
            diff = |fd - g[idx]|
            worst := worst MAX diff
            report(label " P[" idx "] backprop " g[idx] " fd " fd " (golden fd " nums[2] ")", diff, tolFd)
        end
        report(label " worst |fd - backprop|", worst, tolFd)
      end
    checkFd("fd doc 0", goldensDir "/fd_doc0.txt", keys(1, fn (i: ZZ32): ZZ32 => 0), g0)
    checkFd("fd batch 4", goldensDir "/fd_batch4.txt", keys(4, fn (i: ZZ32): ZZ32 => i), g4)
    println "total " ((nanoTime() - wall0) DIV 1000000000) " s"
  end
end

# Run C: design notes

microGPT (Karpathy's 243-line, one-layer, four-head character model) in native
Fortress arrays, with the data laid out after Aaron Hsu's "Designing Your Data"
(Functional Conf 2025), following
`explorations/apl/reference/hsu-flat/microgpt_concise.dyalog` line for line.
Interpreter path only; nothing outside `explorations/run-c/` was changed.
The program is `src/MicroGptFlat.fss` with its API `src/MicroGptFlat.fsi`;
the standard of success is `src/MicroGptFlatCheck.fss`, whose outputs at one
and four threads are in `checks/`.

## The layout

| Hsu's tactic | Dyalog line | in the Fortress program |
|---|---|---|
| 2/8 aggregation, views | `P←⊃,/,¨…` / `v←{(⍵⊃SHP)⍴P[(⍵⊃OFF)+⍳⍵⊃CNT]}` | `p: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]` of 4192 values; `view(p, i)` is a `PView`, a six-line object extending `Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]` whose `get`/`put` address `p[off + i c + j]`. Made in `step` when needed, never stored. |
| 3/5 inverted table, symbol table | `TOKM←↑{(BLK+1)↑BOS,(⎕A⍳⍵),BOS}¨docs ⋄ LEN←1+≢¨docs` | `corpusTokens: Array[\ZZ32,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]` (2000 × 17, filled with 26 then the interned characters), `corpusLengths: Array[\ZZ32,ZZ32\]`; built once at component initialisation by `loadCorpus`. |
| 1 slicing | rows of every activation are (doc, pos) pairs | `x`, `xp`, `x1`, `q`, `kk`, `vv`, `hc`, `x2` … are (B·16 × 16) matrices; every linear map is one library matrix product. |
| 9 Boolean masks | `MK←¯1E10×~(⍳BLK)∘.≥⍳BLK`; `vm×⍟…`; `×M0>0` | `causalMask` is an additive 16 × 16 matrix; `vm` is an RR64 0/1 vector multiplied into the loss and, as `vm / nv`, scaled into `dL`; ReLU's backward is `hadamard(dX4 f2, positive(m0))`. |
| 10 keys | `wte[ids;]`, `(⍉ids∘.=⍳VS)+.×dX` | `ids`, `tg`, `pos` are `Array[\ZZ32,ZZ32\]` key vectors; `gather(wte, ids)` reads rows, `onehot(ids, vocabSize)^T DOT dX` is the scatter-add. |
| lesson 7 lifetimes | `STEP←{…}` pure | `step(p, b): (RR64, Array[\RR64,ZZ32\])`; no activation survives the call, no graph, no cache. |
| lesson 8 functional state | `ADAM` replaces `P M V` | `adam(p, m, v, g, t, lr)` returns three fresh vectors; the training loop's three variables are the only state. |
| lesson 1 data hiding is a myth | `SHP CNT OFF` | `matName`, `matRows`, `matCols`, `matCount`, `matOffset`, `nParams` are six visible one-line functions. |

The layout matches `experiment/run-c-goldens/goldens.json` `layout`: offsets
0, 432, 688, 1120, 1376, 1632, 1888, 2144, 3168; total 4192; each matrix
row-major.

## The step, line for line

| Dyalog | Fortress (`step`) |
|---|---|
| `R←TOKM[b;] ⋄ ids←,R[;⍳BLK] ⋄ tg←,R[;1+⍳BLK]` | `ids = keys(n, fn r => corpusTokens[b[r DIV blockSize], r MOD blockSize])`, `tg` likewise at `+1` |
| `vm←,LEN[b]∘.>⍳BLK ⋄ nv←+/vm ⋄ pos←N⍴⍳BLK` | `vm = vec(n, fn r => if (r MOD blockSize) < corpusLengths[…] then 1.0 else 0.0)`, `nv = SUM[r <- 0#n] vm[r]`, `pos = keys(n, fn r => r MOD blockSize)` |
| `wte wpe lm wq wk wv wo f1 f2←v¨⍳9` | nine `view(p, i)` |
| `X←wte[ids;]+wpe[pos;]` | `x = gather(wte, ids) + gather(wpe, pos)` |
| `Xp←rmsn⍤1⊢X ⋄ X1←rmsn⍤1⊢Xp` | `xp = rmsnRows(x); x1 = rmsnRows(xp)` |
| `Q K Vv←X1∘(+.×⍉)¨wq wk wv` | `q = x1 (wq^T); kk = x1 (wk^T); vv = x1 (wv^T)` |
| `h←{0 2 1 3⍉(B,BLK,NH,HD)⍴⍵} ⋄ Qh Kh Vh←h¨Q K Vv` | no data moves: `head(q, d, h)` is a `Block` view of rows `16d..`, columns `4h..` |
| `A←sm⍤1⊢MK+⍤2⊢(Qh+.×⍤2⊢⍉⍤2⊢Kh)÷HD*0.5` | `for d <- 0#bsz, h <- 0#nHead do … assignInto(ah, smRows((qh (kh^T)) / (SQRT (1.0 headDim)) + causalMask))` |
| `Hc←(N,NE)⍴0 2 1 3⍉A+.×⍤2⊢Vh` | `assignInto(head(hc, d, h), ah vh)` in the same loop |

Departures from the Dyalog, and why:

- `⍉` on the weights is the postfix `^T` (`m.t()`, the library's zero-copy
  `TransposedMatrix`), and `+.×` is the library's juxtaposition product. A
  call result cannot be transposed in place (`onehot(ids, vocabSize)^T` is the
  static error of ledger row 4), so the two one-hots are bound first.
- `⍤2` and `0 2 1 3⍉` (per-head cells) are a loop over (document, head) with
  block views; see the rank-4 decision below.
- `⊃,/,¨` (ravel and catenate the gradients) is nine writes through views of
  the gradient vector: the layout is the same table that reads the weights.
- `tg⌷⍤0 1⊢Pr` is a subscript inside the loss sum; `tg∘.=⍳VS` is `onehot`.
- The Dyalog's `h` makes an array; here `head` and `headCell` make views, so
  `Qh Kh Vh` never exist as values.

## The rank-4 decision

Batch × heads × positions × head-dim is handled by looping over documents and
heads with `Matrix` views of the (doc·pos × 16) activations, not by an
`Array4` object. `Block[\br,bc,r,c\](base, r0, c0)` is six lines and gives
`head(q, d, h)`, a 16 × 4 `Matrix` over rows `16d..16d+15` and columns
`4h..4h+3` of `q`; writing through the same kind of view into `hc`, `dQ`,
`dK`, `dV` is the inverse permutation for free. The B·NH attention matrices
live in one (B·NH·16 × 16) matrix `att` whose cells are `headCell(att, d, h)`.

Reasons:

1. The shipped library stops at rank 3 and has no batched product: an
   `Array4` would need its own `+.×⍤2`, `⍉⍤2` and `sm⍤1` written as loops over
   the leading two axes anyway, so it would buy notation and not reuse.
2. The Dyalog's `0 2 1 3⍉` is a view in Hsu's sense (tactic 8); a block view
   is exactly that, and it moves no data in either direction.
3. Each (document, head) step is two 16 × 4 · 4 × 16 products and a softmax
   on a 16 × 16 matrix through the same `rmsnRows`/`smRows` functions the rest
   of the program uses; nothing is special-cased.
4. The loop is a plain parallel `for` over two generators; each iteration
   writes a disjoint block, so the four-thread run needs no atomics.

The cost is that the attention lines are five statements in a loop rather
than two array expressions.

## What the language gave, what had to be built

Given by the library, used unchanged: `array[\RR64\](n)` and `(r, c)`
runtime-sized arrays that dispatch as `Vector`/`Matrix`; the matrix product in
both spellings; `.t()`; `Matrix + -`; `Vector + - pmul` and scalar scaling;
`SUM` and `BIG MAX` with generator clauses; `exp`, `log`, `SQRT`, `MAX`;
`DIV`/`MOD`; the `reflect`/`N[\n\]` idiom that turns a run-time size into a
`nat`; `FileReadStream.readLine`; `Char.codePoint`; tuple binding and tuple
assignment; parallel `for` over two generators; a component that exports both
`Executable` and its own API.

Built in the component (all user-level): `PView` and `Block` (six lines
each) with their `reflect` wrappers; the postfix `^T`; elementwise `/`, `+`
and `SQRT` on vectors and `/` on a matrix by a scalar (Adam's expressions
and the score scaling); `gather`, `onehot`, `scaleRows`, `hadamard`, `relu`,
`positive`; `rmsnRows`, `rmsnRowsB`, `smRows`, `smRowsB` (row-wise maps: a
per-row vector then a `mat` fill); `assignInto`; a float parser (the
library's `strToFloat` overflows a 32-bit integer on a 17-digit mantissa and
mishandles a sign) and a whitespace tokenizer (`String.split()` is the rope's
structural subdivision, not a tokenizer); a two-pass line loader for the
corpus.

## Numerics

The weights are parsed by accumulating the mantissa's digits in an `RR64`
and dividing by an exact power of ten, which is within one or two units in
the last place of Python's correctly rounded parse; the check component's
first line measures the loaded vector against the goldens' `P0` (the
difference is at that level). The reductions are the library's parallel
`SUM`, so summation order differs from numpy's; the golden comparisons are
at 1e-12 for losses, 1e-12 for the gradient and the Adam step, and 1e-8 for
finite differences, against the measured values recorded in `checks/`.
All arithmetic is `RR64`; care was needed that every value written into an
`RR64` array is a float (`1.0 headDim`, `1.0` and `0.0` in the masks), since
the walk path does not enforce a declared return type.

## Cost

One thread, batch 1: about 8 s per step (forward and backward); batch 4:
see `checks/threads1.txt` for the measured times. The library's product
runs at roughly 24 µs per multiply-add (`probes/p05_mmtime.fss`), and a
hand-written loop is no faster, so the step time is the interpreter's
per-operation cost times the 190K (batch 1) to 750K (batch 4) multiply-adds
of the model. No speed work was done, as the brief asks.

## Blinding

Nothing on the brief's excluded list was opened, and no history was read.
Two things came close and are recorded: `CLAUDE.md` and the gap ledger name
excluded paths (`microgpt-port.md`, `compiled-path-gaps.md`, `run-b/probes/…`)
as citations, which were not followed; and `explorations/apl/README.md`
(rung 6's line in its table) mentions that the APL rungs had exercised "the
program's attention score" and the one-hot scatter-add — a sentence about
the APL work, not the prior Fortress ports. The Hsu handover's tactics
table and the two verified references were the design inputs, as the brief
lists.

step(p: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], b: Array[\ZZ32,ZZ32\]): (RR64, Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]) = do
    bsz = |b|
    n = bsz blockSize
    ids = keys(n, fn (r: ZZ32): ZZ32 => corpusTokens[b[r DIV blockSize], r MOD blockSize])
    tg = keys(n, fn (r: ZZ32): ZZ32 => corpusTokens[b[r DIV blockSize], (r MOD blockSize) + 1])
    vm = vec(n, fn (r: ZZ32): RR64 => if (r MOD blockSize) < corpusLengths[b[r DIV blockSize]] then 1.0 else 0.0 end)
    nv = SUM[r <- 0#n] vm[r]
    pos = keys(n, fn (r: ZZ32): ZZ32 => r MOD blockSize)
    wte = view(p, 0); wpe = view(p, 1); lm = view(p, 2)
    wq = view(p, 3); wk = view(p, 4); wv = view(p, 5); wo = view(p, 6)
    f1 = view(p, 7); f2 = view(p, 8)
    (* -- forward, all (doc,pos) rows at once -- *)
    x = gather(wte, ids) + gather(wpe, pos)
    xp = rmsnRows(x); x1 = rmsnRows(xp)
    q = x1 (wq^T); kk = x1 (wk^T); vv = x1 (wv^T)
    att = zerosM(bsz nHead blockSize, blockSize)
    hc = zerosM(n, nEmbd)
    for d <- 0#bsz, h <- 0#nHead do
        qh = head(q, d, h); kh = head(kk, d, h); vh = head(vv, d, h)
        ah = headCell(att, d, h)
        assignInto(ah, smRows((qh (kh^T)) / (SQRT (1.0 headDim)) + causalMask))
        assignInto(head(hc, d, h), ah vh)
    end
    x2 = xp + hc (wo^T)
    x3 = rmsnRows(x2); m0 = x3 (f1^T); mr = relu(m0)
    x4 = x2 + mr (f2^T)
    pr = smRows(x4 (lm^T))
    loss = -(SUM[r <- 0#n] vm[r] (log(pr[r, tg[r]]))) / nv
    (* -- backward, one line under each forward line, bottom-up -- *)
    g = zeros(nParams())
    dL = scaleRows(vm / nv, pr - onehot(tg, vocabSize))
    assignInto(view(g, 2), (dL^T) x4); dX4 = dL lm
    assignInto(view(g, 8), (dX4^T) mr); dM0 = hadamard(dX4 f2, positive(m0))
    assignInto(view(g, 7), (dM0^T) x3); dX3 = dM0 f1
    dX2 = dX4 + rmsnRowsB(dX3, x2)
    assignInto(view(g, 6), (dX2^T) hc); dH = dX2 wo
    dQ = zerosM(n, nEmbd); dK = zerosM(n, nEmbd); dV = zerosM(n, nEmbd)
    for d <- 0#bsz, h <- 0#nHead do
        ah = headCell(att, d, h); dh = head(dH, d, h)
        qh = head(q, d, h); kh = head(kk, d, h); vh = head(vv, d, h)
        assignInto(head(dV, d, h), (ah^T) dh)
        dS = smRowsB(ah, dh (vh^T)) / (SQRT (1.0 headDim))
        assignInto(head(dQ, d, h), dS kh)
        assignInto(head(dK, d, h), (dS^T) qh)
    end
    assignInto(view(g, 3), (dQ^T) x1); assignInto(view(g, 4), (dK^T) x1); assignInto(view(g, 5), (dV^T) x1)
    dX1 = dQ wq + dK wk + dV wv
    dXp = dX2 + rmsnRowsB(dX1, xp); dX = rmsnRowsB(dXp, x)
    ohIds = onehot(ids, vocabSize); ohPos = onehot(pos, blockSize)
    assignInto(view(g, 0), (ohIds^T) dX)
    assignInto(view(g, 1), (ohPos^T) dX)
    (loss, g)
  end
